label: CONSORT
source: CONSORT statement, https://www.consort-statement.org (pointer only; wording is our own)

items.text: Names the design as a randomised trial and gives a clear summary in the abstract.
Explains the background, the rationale and the specific aims of the trial.
Describes the design, including its allocation ratio and structure.
Says who was eligible and where and when the trial took place.
Describes each intervention in enough detail for someone to repeat it.
Defines the primary and secondary outcomes and when they were measured.
Explains how the sample size was set and any rules for stopping early.
Says how the random sequence was generated.
Explains how the allocation was kept hidden until assignment.
Says who generated the sequence, enrolled people and assigned interventions.
Says who was blinded to allocation, and how.
Lists the methods used to compare the groups.
Shows how many people were screened, randomised, followed up and analysed, ideally in a flow diagram.
Gives the dates of recruitment and follow-up, and why the trial ended or was stopped.
Reports the baseline characteristics of each group.
Gives the number of participants analysed in each group, and why any were left out.
Reports the results for each outcome, with the size and precision of the effect.
Reports any extra analyses, marking which were planned and which were not.
Reports adverse events and harms in each group.
Discusses the trial's limits, including any risk of bias or imprecision.
Discusses how far the results apply to other people and settings.
Gives a cautious reading of the results in light of the evidence.
Gives the trial registry name and the registration number.
Says where the full trial protocol can be read.
Names the funders and their role in the trial.
